ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $ \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF $, with B, E, C, F lying on the same straight line. If $ BF = 8\text{cm} $ and $ BE = 2\text{cm} $, then what is the length of $ CE $ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF$,\\
it follows that $BC = EF$,\\
therefore $BC - CE = EF - CE$,\\
hence $BE = CF$,\\
given that $BE = 2\text{cm}$,\\
it implies $CF = BE = 2\text{cm}$,\\
since $BF = 8\text{cm}$,\\
thus $CE = BF - BE - CF = 8 - 2 - 2 = \boxed{4}\text{cm}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the bottom edge is a horizontal straight line, and the points are labeled B, E, C, F in order from left to right. On the left there is triangle ABC, where B and C are on the bottom line, and A is above; on the right there is triangle DEF, where E and F are on the same bottom line, and D is above. The problem gives \triangle ABC \cong \triangle DEF. Reasoning: From the corresponding order of the congruent triangles, side BC and side EF correspond and are equal, so BC = EF. According to the order of the points on the bottom line B-E-C-F, BC = BE + CE, EF = CE + CF. Substituting BC = EF gives BE + CE = CE + CF; canceling CE gives BE = CF. It is known that BE = 2 cm, so CF = 2 cm. Also BF is the whole segment, BF = BE + CE + CF = 8 cm, therefore CE = 8 - 2 - 2 = 4 cm.
